jobs.occupation: Experienced High Voltage Specialist wanted for Bravida El-Infrastruktur Øst

jobs.occupation: Communications Student Assistant – Partnerships, Advocacy and Communications Team
jobs.description:
About ICARS    The International Centre for Antimicrobial Resistance Solutions (ICARS) is an independent international organisation established by the Danish Government to support low- and middle-income countries in developing evidence-based and context-appropriate solutions to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Working across the One Health spectrum, ICARS collaborates with governments, research institutions and global organisations to bridge research, policy and implementation.    About the role   We are looking for a Student Assistant to join our Partnerships, Advocacy and Communications Team. This is a great opportunity for a student interested in digital communications, creative media, data management and global health and development. You’ll support our day-to-day activities and help communicate ICARS’ work on AMR in LMICs.   We’re looking for someone with strong technical skills who also takes initiative to bring fresh ideas to the team. Alongside delivering assigned tasks, you will be encouraged to suggest improvements and take ownership of agreed activities, with support and feedback from colleagues.      Key responsibilities    Website management:    	
•  	Maintain and update content on ICARS’ WordPress website, keeping it accurate, accessible and user-friendly.  	    	
•  	Track website performance using analytics tools and suggest improvements based on the findings.  	    	
•  	Proactively identify outdated content, gaps and opportunities to better showcase our work.  	   Graphic design & visual content:    	
•  	Create engaging infographics, social media graphics and report layouts that align with ICARS’ brand.  	    	
•  	Help develop templates and designs for reports and presentations, bringing fresh ideas for communicating complex information clearly.  	    	
•  	Video editing & multimedia:  	    	
•  	Edit videos for ICARS’ social media, presentations and events.  	    	
•  	Support video production and identify opportunities to turn existing footage into useful, engaging content.  	   Social media support :    	
•  	Support ICARS’ LinkedIn presence through content creation and community engagement.  	    	
•  	Keep an eye on relevant conversations, project updates and sector developments, suggesting timely stories and opportunities for ICARS to contribute.  	   Internal communications support:    	
•  	Maintain our internal SharePoint, including keeping our media library organised and up to date.  	    	
•  	Support colleagues with designing clear, engaging PowerPoint slides and formatting Word documents.  	   Press Office and external communications support:    	
•  	Assist with event promotion and Mailchimp newsletter creation.  	    	
•  	Monitor our communications mailbox, respond to routine enquiries and coordinate with colleagues on requests from stakeholders, including regional and national press.  	    	
•  	Flag relevant media and communications opportunities for the team to consider.  	   Data and stakeholder information management:    	
•  	Support the team in entering and maintaining accurate, up-to-date data and contact information in ATLAS, our CRM system.  	    	
•  	Other tasks related to deliverables of the Partnerships, Advocacy and Communications Team.   	      Desired profile    We are seeking an organised and curious student who enjoys both developing ideas and getting things done in a pro-active and structured manner. You take the initiative to find information, ask useful questions and suggest practical next steps. You can work independently, recognise when to seek guidance and lead tasks through to completion, while keeping colleagues informed. You are comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly, and you bring strong digital fluency, technical skills and the ability to pick up new tools with ease.   Required qualifications:    	
•  	Currently studying for a Master’s degree in IT, Media Studies, Marketing, Graphic Design or a related field.  	    	
•  	Proficiency in WordPress and basic website management.  	    	
•  	Experience using MS Office, particularly Excel, Word and PowerPoint.  	    	
•  	Experience with graphic design tools, such as Canva or Adobe Creative Suite.  	    	
•  	Basic video editing skills, using Premiere Pro, Final Cut or similar software.  	    	
•  	Strong organisational skills, working in a structured manner and with attention to detail.  	    	
•  	Ability to prioritise and manage multiple tasks.  	    	
•  	Ability to identify opportunities, propose ideas and take responsibility for delivering agreed tasks.  	    	
•  	Strong written and verbal communication skills in perfect and fluent English, including the ability to adapt content for different audiences.  	   Preferred qualifications:    	
•  	Knowledge of Google Analytics, or a willingness to learn.  	    	
•  	Experience using CRM platforms (Dynamics 365)  	    	
•  	Skills and interest in drafting technical and scientific communication material.  	      What we offer     	
•  	Hands-on experience: Contribute to drafting communications material, external stakeholder management and partnerships, developing your skills through practical work and feedback.  	    	
•  	Impact: Help communicate solutions to one of the world’s most critical global health and development challenges, with space to contribute your own ideas and see them put into practice.  	    	
•  	Flexible working hours: Our working hours between 8 am and 5 pm with accommodation of your academic schedule.  	    	
•  	International environment: Work alongside experts and colleagues from diverse backgrounds in a global organisation.  	   If you enjoy turning ideas into action and want to use your communications skills to support global health, we would love to hear from you!      Terms of employment   The position as student assistant will be covered by the terms of the collective agreement between The Danish Finance Ministry and the Organisation of Public Employees (OAO-S-Fællesoverenskomsten) and the organizational agreement between The Danish Finance Ministry and the Organisation for Salaried Employees HK/Stat (Organisationsaftale for kontorfunktionærer, laboranter og it-medarbejdere (HK)), according to chapter 6 in the agreement concerning hourly paid employees.   The successful candidate is enrolled at graduate level in a Danish University with at around two years of studies remaining. They will predominantly work from the ICARS HQ office, based at the Statens Serum Institut in Copenhagen, Denmark.      Application and recruitment process     Press “apply for the position” and submit your CV along with a cover letter outlining your suitability for the role and motivation for applying.     We would like to receive your application by 20 November 2026 and expect to conduct interviews 24-27 November 2026.   For questions about the role, please contact Communications Officer Chloe Modvig-Cole (checo@icars-global.org) and for other questions about the position you may contact Head of Partnerships and Global Relations Theresa Hogenhaug (tcah@icars-global.org). We are committed to cultivating a fair and healthy environment, where everyone can be themselves and thrive. We are happy to discuss flexible working options for all roles. We work to ensure that our recruitment processes are as inclusive as possible to everyone. This includes adjusting for people who have a disability or long-term condition.   We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.occupation: Embedded Software & Control Engineer
jobs.description: Job description:Do you enjoy writing C++ software that interacts directly with hardware and makes complex systems perform reliably in the real world?At Robotto, we build advanced autonomy and software solutions for drones and unmanned systems. Our work brings together computer vision, embedded software, control, electronics and real-world product development.We are looking for an Embedded Software Engineer with strong C++ experience to develop software close to the hardware layer of our drone platform. Experience with motor control and Field-Oriented Control (FOC) is highly preferred.This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working at the intersection of software, electronics and control systems, where performance, reliability and real-world behaviour matter.The role:You will work on embedded software that supports the control and operation of Robotto's drone and unmanned systems.Your work will involve developing reliable C++ software that interfaces with hardware, sensors, motors and other system components. You will work closely with colleagues across control, electronics, computer vision and flight testing to take software from development through integration and into real-world operation.For candidates with motor-control experience, you will also have the opportunity to contribute to the development and improvement of our motor-control capabilities, including Field-Oriented Control (FOC).What you will do:- Develop and maintain embedded software in C++ for drones and unmanned systems.- Build software that interfaces with motors, sensors, actuators and other hardware components.- Work with real-time and performance-sensitive software.- Contribute to motor-control software, including Field-Oriented Control (FOC), where relevant to your experience.- Develop and integrate communication between embedded components and wider product systems.- Debug complex software and hardware interactions and identify root causes of issues.- Collaborate closely with control, electronics, flight-test and software engineers.- Contribute to software architecture, testing, documentation, code quality and technical decisions.- Support integration and testing on real hardware and drone platforms.What success could look like in your first 3-6 months:- You have developed a strong understanding of Robotto's embedded architecture, hardware and control systems.- You are contributing production-quality C++ code to our embedded platform.- You are successfully integrating and debugging software on real hardware.- You are contributing to improved reliability and performance across our embedded systems.- If you have motor-control experience, you are actively contributing to our FOC and motor-control development.- You have become a trusted technical partner for colleagues across software, control, electronics and flight testing.What we are looking for:We are looking for an engineer who is comfortable working close to hardware and enjoys solving complex technical problems where software and physical systems meet.- At least 3 years of professional software engineering experience, ideally within embedded or real-time systems.- Experience with motor control, particularly Field-Oriented Control (FOC), is highly preferred. Experience with BLDC/PMSM motors, control loops, PWM, encoders or related motor-control technologies would also be highly relevant.- Strong C++ programming skills.- Hands-on experience developing software that interfaces with hardware.- Experience with embedded systems, real-time systems, microcontrollers or similar low-level environments.- Good understanding of debugging, testing, software architecture and version control.- Experience with communication protocols such as CAN, UART, SPI, I²C or similar is an advantage.- Experience with robotics, drones, autonomous systems or other complex electromechanical products is an advantage.- Professional fluency in English.- A degree in computer science, software engineering, electrical engineering, robotics, mechatronics or a related field is preferred; equivalent practical experience is equally welcome.Who you are:You are practical, curious and comfortable getting close to both the software and the hardware when solving a problem.- You take ownership of your work and care about software quality and reliability.- You enjoy understanding how systems behave beyond the code itself.- You approach debugging methodically and are comfortable solving difficult software/hardware problems.- You collaborate well across software, electronics and control disciplines.- You are comfortable working in a fast-moving environment with evolving priorities.- You communicate technical trade-offs, progress and risks clearly and pragmatically.Minds and makers forging ahead together.At Robotto, we value people who do. People who take ownership, are willing to try new things just to see if they work, and are comfortable asking for forgiveness rather than permission. We want people who are curious, proactive and excited about turning ideas into something real.Why join Robotto?Robotto is building advanced autonomy technology for drones and unmanned systems, working at the intersection of software, hardware, computer vision, control and real-world operations.You will join a highly technical and ambitious team at an exciting point in the company's journey. As we continue to scale our engineering team and work on challenging new projects, you will have the opportunity to influence how our embedded and control software develops.This is a role where your software will not remain behind a screen. You will see it integrated with real hardware, tested on real systems and used in demanding real-world environments.You will work closely with talented engineers, take meaningful technical ownership and help shape the next generation of Robotto's technology.Equal Employment Opportunity:Robotto is committed to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering an inclusive workplace. We recruit based on skills, experience and potential. Please note that certain positions may require specific nationality or eligibility for security clearance in accordance with applicable laws and the nature of our work.More information and application:https://careers.robotto.ai/jobs/8273412-embedded-software-control-engineer

contribute to the software that connects and powers different parts of Robotto's technology platform.This is a hands-on software engineering role for someone who enjoys building reliable systems, solving complex technical problems and seeing their software move beyond development into real-world operation.The role:You will develop and maintain C++ software across Robotto's software ecosystem, jobs.occupation: Lead Game Programmer
jobs.description: Do you love designing clean game architecture, building multiplayer systems that run smoothly, and helping a team of programmers make the right technical decisions? Great! platform services such as GameKit and the Game Controller framework using Xcode and SwiftExperience with backend services, dedicated servers or cloud hosting for online gamesInterest in multiplayer game design and social featuresExperience working with automated build pipelines such as JenkinsExperience building systemic or open-world gamesWhat always matters to us at TribandYou thrive in taking ownership of your area: you spot problems, seek advice when needed, and implement creative solutions that push projects forwardYou're motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness and creativity while actively contributing to sustaining that cultureYou believe games are made by teams, not rockstars and that great ideas can come from anyoneYou bring curiosity, generosity, and jobs.occupation: Research Assistant in Artificial Intelligence for Power Electronics Design
jobs.description:
At AAU Energy, a fixed-term position as Research Assistant in Artificial Intelligence for Power Electronics Design, is open for appointment from January 1, 2027, or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is 2 years.

Your work tasksYour work will include developing, training and evaluating machine-learning models based on circuit data, board geometries, simulation results and design images. You will develop surrogate models that approximate thermal and electromagnetic solvers, enabling faster evaluation of design alternatives. The position may also involve computer vision for recognizing circuit structures, component placements and printed circuit board geometries from photographs or other images. In addition, you will investigate graph-based methods for representing circuit relationships, evaluating design rules and generating or testing hypotheses for circuit designs. You will contribute to the development and verification of agentic workflows, where artificial intelligence systems combine models, tools and design rules to reason through and support electronics design tasks. You will prepare datasets, document computational workflows, validate model performance and share results with colleagues working in artificial intelligence, power electronics, semiconductors and software development.

The position is offered within the research field of Artificial Intelligence for Power Electronics Design and contributes to AAU Energy’s focus areas of Digital Transformation and Artificial Intelligence, and Energy Efficiency in Components and Systems. The Research Assistant will be affiliated with the Section of Power Electronics System Integration and Materials.

Your competenciesYou have a relevant master’s degree in computer science, electrical engineering, electronics, artificial intelligence or a related field, and you are interested in working at the intersection of machine learning and power electronics design. You have a solid foundation in applied machine learning. Familiarity with electronic systems, including printed circuit boards, circuit topologies, components and the physical principles that influence electrical, thermal and electromagnetic performance, will help you engage with the engineering context of the role.

You have practical experience developing, training and evaluating machine-learning models, and you can translate complex engineering challenges into data-driven methods suited to a research environment. You are comfortable working with structured and unstructured engineering data, including circuit representations, board geometries, simulation data and images. Experience with computer vision, graph-based machine learning or graph neural networks will support your work with methods that interpret circuit layouts and geometries, reason about relationships between components, and generate or assess design hypotheses.

You are interested in developing surrogate models that approximate thermal and electromagnetic simulation tools while maintaining sufficient accuracy for use in electronics-design workflows. You work systematically with model validation, data quality and reproducible experiments, and you understand that artificial intelligence methods for engineering need to be technically robust as well as useful to domain specialists.

You communicate clearly in English, both in writing and dialogue, and you work well in a multidisciplinary environment where colleagues with expertise in artificial intelligence, power electronics and software development collaborate closely. You take responsibility for your tasks, ask constructive questions when assumptions need clarification, and contribute with curiosity and sound technical judgement to the development of new methods for intelligent electronic-system design.

Who we areAAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners and other academic environments to address real-world energy challenges.

The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and from a broad range of national backgrounds. This creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as the working language in research and teaching, which makes it straightforward for international colleagues to integrate.

We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday work.

New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters. Aalborg University offers general onboarding support to all new employees, as well as dedicated support for international staff through its International Staff Unit (ISU). You can read more about relocation support and services here: https://www.en.hr.aau.dk/relocation-support

Aalborg University also offers Danish language courses to support international employees in settling into both the workplace and Danish society. International employees typically can attend Danish language courses during their first years in Denmark (depending on individual eligibility and national schemes).

You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk

Qualification requirements Appointment as a research assistant requires academic qualifications at master's degree level.How to apply  Your application must include the following: 

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position. 
• Curriculum Vitae (CV). 
• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and potential PhD diploma). 
• Documentation of teaching qualifications (optional). 
• Additional qualifications in relation to the position. 
• References/recommendations. 
You can read more about the requirements for your application here.    

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.  

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. 

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society. 

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment. 

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.    

Selected candidates will be invited for an interview. Interviews are expected to be held during December 2026

Further information Read more about our recruitment process here   

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.  

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace. 

Salary and terms of employment  The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Research assistant”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the worldAalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.
